favourite.heading: Why Auburn can pull away
bullets: Playing at Auburn is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Auburn by 1.8 points: ball control vs front disruption (+1.8 pts).

Auburn is the better football team by 1.5 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+1.5 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Florida can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -15.6 to p90 +28.4 for Auburn, so a projection of +7.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.

The market disagrees by 9.9 points. The market is not the truth, but a gap that large is more often the model missing information (a suspension, a starter, a scheme change) than the market being wrong.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk makes it Auburn -7.4 where the market has Auburn +2.5 at captured (stale 157h) · FanDuel — a 9.9 points disagreement. EdgeDesk prices this game at Auburn -7.4 with a fair total of 52.1, which makes Auburn the better team here by that margin on this field.
lessons.actual_result: Auburn Tigers lost by 5. Auburn Tigers lost by 5 where EdgeDesk projected a 7.4-point edge.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Auburn as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 17.3 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 7 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 51.9.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 83 points, an error of 31.1.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Auburn -7.4 where the market has Auburn +2.5 at captured (stale 157h) · FanDuel — a 9.9 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Auburn Tigers lost by 5. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
